title: Rajinikanth Dethrones Vijay With Rs 1,981 Crore Post-COVID Gross as Jailer 2 Roars
excerpt: Jailer 2's Rs 425.89 crore opening weekend lifted Rajinikanth's five-film post-COVID worldwide total to Rs 1,981.01 crore, past Thalapathy Vijay's Rs 1,909.95 crore.
body:
• Rajinikanth's five post-COVID releases have grossed Rs 1,981.01 crore worldwide, overtaking Thalapathy Vijay's Rs 1,909.95 crore from five releases, according to Koimoi box office tracking.
  • Jailer 2 delivered the decisive push, grossing Rs 425.89 crore worldwide in just four days — also Kollywood's biggest opening weekend on record, per Koimoi.
  • Four of Rajinikanth's five post-COVID films crossed Rs 250 crore worldwide: Jailer (Rs 609.29 crore), Coolie (Rs 516.81 crore), Vettaiyan (Rs 255.33 crore) and Jailer 2, with Annaatthe the lowest at Rs 173.69 crore.
  • At 75, Rajinikanth is now within striking distance of becoming Kollywood's first actor to gross Rs 2,000 crore worldwide in the post-COVID era.

Rajinikanth has overtaken Thalapathy Vijay to become Kollywood's highest-grossing leading star of the post-COVID era, after the opening weekend of Jailer 2 pushed his cumulative worldwide gross to Rs 1,981.01 crore across five releases.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=m7cn_dqeL2E

The milestone, tracked by Koimoi, ends Vijay's hold on the record. Vijay had grossed Rs 1,909.95 crore across his own five post-COVID releases. Jailer 2, which grossed Rs 425.89 crore worldwide in four days, supplied the margin that finally carried Rajinikanth past him — by Rs 71.06 crore, with the film still in the opening phase of its run.

How the Rs 1,981 crore was built

Rajinikanth's post-COVID run began modestly by his standards. Annaatthe, his first release of the era, grossed Rs 173.69 crore worldwide. The rebound came with Jailer, which grossed Rs 609.29 crore and remains the biggest single contributor to his total. Vettaiyan followed with Rs 255.33 crore, and Coolie added Rs 516.81 crore last year.

"Jailer 2 delivered the decisive push, grossing Rs 425.89 crore worldwide in just four days — also Kollywood's biggest opening weekend on record, per Koimoi."

https://x.com/Koimoi/status/2112154294371693047

Jailer 2 is the accelerant. Its Rs 425.89 crore in four days made it, according to Koimoi, the highest-grossing South Indian film of 2026 so far, ahead of Ram Charan's Peddi at Rs 341.15 crore, and the first South Indian film to cross Rs 400 crore worldwide this year. Koimoi breaks Jailer 2's four-day worldwide gross down as Rs 235.89 crore gross in India and Rs 190 crore overseas.

The India net picture tells a tighter race

Worldwide gross is only one of the two scoreboards. In India net collections — the measure Indian trade trackers quote most often — Rajinikanth has crossed a different milestone but has not yet taken Vijay's crown. His five post-COVID films total Rs 1,031.82 crore net in India: Annaatthe Rs 106.77 crore, Jailer Rs 348.55 crore, Vettaiyan Rs 146.89 crore, Coolie Rs 285.01 crore and Jailer 2 Rs 144.6 crore in its first three days, according to Koimoi.

That made him only the second Kollywood star, after Vijay, to enter the Rs 1,000 crore net club in India in the post-COVID era, Zoom TV reported. Vijay still leads the India net table at Rs 1,100.71 crore — a gap of Rs 68.89 crore that Jailer 2's continuing run is positioned to close.

Why this record matters

Box office records of this kind are cumulative, not per-film, and they reward something rarer than a single blockbuster: repeatability. Four of Rajinikanth's five releases in this period crossed Rs 250 crore worldwide, a consistency no other Tamil leading man of his generation has matched in the post-pandemic market.

The context sharpens the achievement. Rajinikanth is 75, more than five decades into his career, and competing in an era when Vijay — who has stepped away from cinema for politics, with Jana Nayagan described by Koimoi as his swansong — will not add to his total. Every further crore Jailer 2 earns widens a lead that, barring a Vijay return to films, cannot be chased down by its previous holder.

For diaspora audiences, the overseas numbers explain part of the story: Rs 190 crore of Jailer 2's four-day gross came from outside India, underlining how much of Kollywood's top end now runs through screens in the United States, the Gulf, Malaysia and Singapore.

What happens next

Rajinikanth needs less than Rs 19 crore more in worldwide gross to become Kollywood's first actor to reach Rs 2,000 crore in the post-COVID era — a threshold Koimoi expects him to cross within days on Jailer 2's current trajectory, with Rs 2,100 crore and beyond in play if the film holds. On the India net side, the remaining question is timing: whether Jailer 2 takes him past Vijay's Rs 1,100.71 crore and on toward the Rs 1,200 crore mark Koimoi projects.

Either way, the post-COVID hierarchy in Tamil cinema now has a new name at the top of its worldwide table — and it is the oldest star in the contest.
